info.title: Ploid Public API
info.description: Ploid's focused agent-native people API. Start with 50 ACU for 30 days after creating an account.

post.summary: Find candidate identities in the people index for 1 ACU
post.description: Return up to 10 basic indexed profiles matching all name terms (common given-name variants such as Tim/Timothy included) plus optional company, location, and title filters. The company filter matches the employer exactly, including its aliases (Apple, Apple Inc.), never a namesake (Apple Bank). Requires people:search; legacy full-access keys with both people:enrich and agent:chat are accepted. Costs 1 ACU per completed search, including zero matches; failed searches are not charged. Never starts research or enrichment. Normal account billing, auto-recharge settings, and API-key spending caps apply. Send an Idempotency-Key to replay a request without another charge. Indexed identities and employment are unverified: identity_verified is always false, and profile_url carries a non-LinkedIn profile only (null when LinkedIn is the only one). Ask the user to choose before POST /v1/person, which costs 25 ACU unless the workspace already has active access. Bounded index requests (one, plus a retry per common given-name variant when the spelling finds nobody) for the single charge; no exhaustive count or pagination. Workspace limits: 30 requests/minute and 300/hour across keys. Active account eligibility still applies.

post.summary: Run a task with Ploid SHN-1
post.description: Ploid SHN-1 — Intelligence over the world's information. OpenAI-compatible chat completion where the model is an autonomous research agent: the last user message is the task, earlier turns are context, and `input_file` parts land in the agent's workspace. The agent searches the web, Ploid's people and company data and the files, runs code in a sandbox, checks its sources and answers with citations. Runs take minutes, so use `stream: true`: progress arrives as `reasoning` deltas, the answer as `content`, and the last chunk carries `usage` and a `ploid` block with output files. One run costs a flat fee in ACU; Ploid data the agent uses inside the run is metered to your workspace at normal prices. Datasets and Sets remain available but SHN-1 is the recommended way to run research tasks. Idempotency-Key is not supported on this route. `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens`, `temperature`, `user` and `metadata` are accepted for SDK compatibility and ignored: the agent chooses its own answer length.

200.description: Completed JSON response (stream=false) or OpenAI-compatible SSE ending in data: [DONE] (stream=true).

schema.description: chat.completion.chunk frames: reasoning deltas for progress, content for the answer, a final chunk with usage and ploid.files, then data: [DONE].

post.summary: Search people synchronously
post.description: Retrieve up to 150 people inline per request; async:true or a larger num_results starts a background People Set instead and returns 202 with set_id, items_url and events_url. instant returns indexed candidates as ranked by the index. fast compiles the query, reads a pool of at least 200 indexed candidates (three times num_results when that is larger) and ranks them by the stated role, place, employer, keywords, industry and seniority before returning the first num_results, without web verification. auto and deep research the complete query and explicit filters before returning matches with verification references; uncertain and rejected candidates are excluded from results, grounding and billing. Auto/deep compile the query, verify candidates, and run one bounded web recovery pass when too few match. Each verification pass permits up to 30 seconds for auto or 45 seconds for deep; recovery discovery permits 45 or 60 seconds respectively; the whole verification stage answers within 60 seconds for auto and 120 seconds for deep. A partial status means the requested count was not filled or verification hit its deadline; coverage.has_more says more candidates remained. Use Sets for durable research of large result sets. Verification is evidence-based model assessment, separate from identity verification. Requires people:search.

post.summary: Get an evidence-backed person record
post.description: Resolve one reviewed person profile. Set type to standard for lighter research (10 ACU) or leave the default deep (25 ACU); a standard receipt upgraded to deep is charged the 15 ACU difference and restarts the 90-day window, and a deep receipt also covers standard rereads. Optionally set include to work_email, personal_email, and/or phone to add a per-request contact lookup. Each found contact is billed at the /v1/enrich price (1, 3, and 10 credits respectively); missing or unavailable contacts are free, and the 90-day profile reread does not make contacts free. Set include to personal_interests for free, evidence-backed personal interests in signals.personal_interests (not gift ideas); signals.affinities is a reserved empty array. This requires a current company and excludes family, health, religion, and politics. Optional goal, website_url and up to 10 anchors (public https URLs the caller says belong to the person) start a private research run that is never served from or saved to the shared stored profile; anchors are trusted as the caller's statement. Reviewed publications, patents, open-source work and media appearances are returned as structured entries in research, work and media; the same claims also appear in summary. An eligible cached profile returns 200, including stale data with a queued refresh. Unseen people and snapshots requiring new review return a durable 202 run. Fresh research can take minutes; poll the returned run ID. A completed uncertain identity returns data:null with meta.resolution=unsure and reason ambiguous_identity or insufficient_evidence. The first successful profile is charged its level price on every plan; organization-wide rereads at the same or a lower level are free for 90 days. Failed, uncertain, and not-found runs are free. Current headline, company and location come only from reviewed evidence (a source-dated status, the profile's own identity claim or headline with no stated period, or an open-ended employment period); age and social audience/activity metrics are not populated by the current reviewed projection. meta.research reports the reviewed status and, when partial, the sections without accepted evidence.

post.summary: Detect a website's technology stack with evidence
post.description: Beta. Returns the technologies found on a domain's website and in its public DNS, one record per technology and scope, each with an assessment and up to five evidence items. tech_id may change during the beta. A stored scan of the same domain is served (source cache) when it is assessed or partial with at least one page captured and no older than freshness.max_age_days (default 30), blocked and under 24 hours old, or failed and under 10 minutes old; a scan under 10 minutes old is served even with max_age_days 0. Once a website opts out of crawling, its stored scans are no longer served, and a domain that opted out answers blocked, free. Otherwise the site is scanned (source scan) within 25 seconds. Live scans are limited per workspace: 2 at once and 200 started per rolling hour (429 scan_capacity_exceeded with Retry-After past either; a retryable 503 and an opted-out domain's blocked answer do not count toward the hourly quota, technographics_scan_failed does). Cached results are not limited. Costs 1 ACU per billable result, scanned or cached alike: one with at least one website page captured (coverage.pages above 0) and at least one website record that is not inferred. Every other result is free, including DNS-only, blocked, failed and empty ones, and so is every error but billing_unavailable, whose charge could not be confirmed; meta.credits_charged shows the charge. Negotiated per-domain prices apply. Every request needs one domain's price in the workspace balance (else 402 insufficient_acu) and within the API key's daily and monthly budgets (else 402 daily_budget_exceeded or monthly_budget_exceeded) before it runs; nothing is charged when the result is free. Included on the Scale plan and Custom agreements; other plans get 403 plan_upgrade_required. Requires people:search.

post.summary: Find trade and hourly workers by role and place
post.description: Staffing search for trade and hourly roles (forklift operators, electricians, welders, CDL drivers, CNAs, …). One role and one place in; the people whose current title names that job, or an adjacent job in the same trade family, in that place or a town within the radius out, best fits first and one row per person. The role is expanded to the titles that mean the same job (reach truck operator, lift truck operator, …) and the place to the towns within radius_miles, so one call replaces a search per title and per town. Synchronous and index-only: titles and places are read as indexed, with no evidence verification. Candidates come from the maintained people index and, unless sources excludes it, a historical archive of US Facebook profiles whose workplace names the trade (rows marked source facebook, freshness archived). Pass person_id to /v1/enrich for contact details. Billed per returned worker like /v1/search. The workspaceId path segment must be the calling key's own workspace id or slug. Requires people:search.

post.summary: Fill typed columns for seeded rows
post.description: Seed up to 25 rows (sync) or 2000 rows (async) of people, companies, or custom entities, and name up to 30 columns. Every cell is fused from many sources into one answer with a 0..1 confidence and public evidence URLs. Sync requests answer within deadline_ms (default 20000); cells still running at the deadline return status timeout. mode async returns 202 and fills rows in the background; poll GET /v1/datasets/{id} and page rows_url. Pay on hit: 1 ACU per 10 found standard cells (rounded up per request), 1 ACU per found custom cell, 1 ACU per work email, 3 ACU per personal email, 10 ACU per phone. not_found, unverified, and timeout cells are free. The API key reserves the all-found upper bound and releases the rest after the run. Requires people:search.

post.summary: Search GitHub accounts by company, repository, activity, language, and profile flags
post.description: Filter Ploid's GitHub accounts index. Every criterion is AND; give at least one. Results come back by relevance when query or company is set, otherwise by merged pull requests and then commits; sort picks an activity ranking instead. Page with offset up to 1000 results deep; the last page before that shrinks to fit, so next_offset can always be followed with the same limit. With include_profiles, each account also carries its live public GitHub profile (limit defaults to and may not exceed 10). Costs 1 ACU per completed search plus 1 ACU per live profile found, charged together; failed searches are not charged. Emails and phone numbers are never returned. Requires people:search.

post.summary: Search people
post.description: People search answered only from the licensed people corpus. Send either a plain-English `query` or structured `filters`. A search the corpus does not answer (for example a person's name alone, or a failed read) is refused with `search_not_answered`; it is never answered as a different search. One credit per ten people returned. Requires the linkedin:read scope.

post.summary: Enrich one person
post.description: Resolve contact fields for one person using a LinkedIn URL, permanent person_id, email (with first and last name at a work domain, or alone for a reverse lookup), or name plus company domain. Request work_email, personal_email, phone, and/or linkedin_url (the profile behind an email: a reverse lookup answered from Ploid's graph in under a second when the email is on file, else from the contact network); every field reports found, not_found, or unavailable with confidence, source, and last_seen. Responses include explicit usage.billed and usage.not_found. The legacy lightweight LinkedIn profile contract remains supported; use /v1/person for deep public evidence. Requires the people:enrich scope.

http_status.description: Semantic status when an error terminates a response after streaming headers opened.

unavailable_fields.description: Requested enrichment fields that could not complete. Present when all requested fields are unavailable.

messages.description: system/developer messages are instructions, the last user message is the task, earlier turns are context. Content is a string or parts of type text or input_file (filename + base64 file_data).

run_id.description: Use with GET /v1/chat/completions/{id} to re-attach for 24 hours.

seq.description: Stream only: sequence of the last stored chunk, for `after` on re-attach.

model.description: Ploid Atlas uses Luna; Ploid Ox uses Sol.

HarnessChatCompletionResponse.description: OpenAI-compatible completion payload with internal model/provider routing metadata removed.

query.description: Optional semantic query. Supply this, at least one structured filter, or both.

type.description: instant returns indexed candidates; fast compiles the query and ranks a pool of at least 200 indexed candidates (three times num_results when larger) by it, without web verification. auto and deep require evidence-backed matches to the complete query and filters; deep also always runs public-web grounding. Verification may return fewer results within its deadline; Sets supports durable research for larger requests.

num_results.description: Up to 150 return inline. Larger requests run as a background People Set (self-serve up to 500).

offset.description: Skip this many ranked matches: num_results 25 with offset 25 is the second page. Pages share the 150-result inline cap and meta.next_offset is set while more remain. instant and fast only; auto, deep and background Sets return 422 unsupported_pagination.

criteria.description: Plain-English conditions every result must satisfy, such as 'Has founded a venture-backed company'. Each is researched and judged separately; results carry one verification entry per criterion and are ranked by evidence strength across all of them. Requires type auto or deep. In async searches they replace the criteria derived from the query.

async.description: Run as a background People Set and return 202 with set_id. Defaults to true above 150 results; false with a larger num_results is rejected. Async searches always verify each row, so type and contents do not apply.

webhook_url.description: Async searches only. Receives the Set's progress events.

filters.description: Hard filters, combined with AND, and enforced on every result. A row that contradicts one is dropped, and a row missing a filtered value is excluded. Each field takes one value, or { any_of, none_of }: any_of is OR, none_of drops a row whose stated value matches. title is a current-role match (word boundaries; a support role or an org name that only contains the word does not count). company is the current employer after legal-suffix normalization; Meta/Facebook, X/Twitter, and Google/Alphabet match. location must contain each place component, and short codes match whole tokens. seniority and industry match indexed fields only. company.employee_count, company.funding_stage, company_size, experience, and education are proven per person with cited evidence: they count toward the criteria limit and need type auto or deep or an async search. company_domain is matched by its brand label against the current employer name (stripe.com matches Stripe); give company or company_domain, not both. radius_km and tenure return 422 unsupported_filters and are never ignored. Each result's filter_match says how every filter was met.

title.description: Current job title must hold this role, or one of any_of.

any_of.description: Matches when the field holds any of these values.

none_of.description: Drops a row whose stated value matches any of these; a missing value is not an exclusion.

seniority.description: Indexed seniority or title must match. Recognized levels: entry, junior, mid, senior, staff, principal, director, vp, cxo.

any_of.description: Matches when the field holds any of these values.

none_of.description: Drops a row whose stated value matches any of these; a missing value is not an exclusion.

company.description: Current employer name. Legal suffixes are ignored; a longer or different name does not match.

any_of.description: Matches when the field holds any of these values.

none_of.description: Drops a row whose stated value matches any of these; a missing value is not an exclusion.

employee_count.description: Current employer headcount, verified with evidence.

funding_stage.description: Current employer's latest funding stage, verified with evidence.

industry.description: Indexed industry must contain this value. Results without an indexed industry cannot satisfy it.

any_of.description: Matches when the field holds any of these values.

none_of.description: Drops a row whose stated value matches any of these; a missing value is not an exclusion.

location.description: City, state, or country must contain this place. State names and postal abbreviations match.

any_of.description: Matches when the field holds any of these values.

none_of.description: Drops a row whose stated value matches any of these; a missing value is not an exclusion.

countries.description: Joined with cities and any_of as alternatives.

cities.description: Joined with countries and any_of as alternatives.

company_size.description: Current employer headcount, verified with evidence. Same as company.employee_count.

experience.description: A past role (not only the current one) at one of these companies, verified with evidence.

education.description: Attended one of these schools, verified with evidence.

company_domain.description: Current employer by website: the domain's brand label is matched as the company name (stripe.com matches Stripe). Give company or company_domain, not both. POST /v1/search only.

freshness.description: How recently the facts behind each result must have been confirmed. max_age_days caps the age of cached evidence for every candidate: 0 means always re-read live sources. Omitted, verification picks a window per request from the time-sensitive facts it depends on (current role, location) and refreshes only the top-ranked candidates. Requires verification: type auto or deep, or an async search; instant and fast return 422 unsupported_freshness. Tighter windows cost more live reads and can return fewer results within the deadline. The response echoes the applied window under request.freshness.

max_age_days.description: Maximum age, in days, of the cached evidence behind each returned result.

fields.description: Which person fields to return. positions, education and photo add the work history, schools and photo_url from our people data; a person we hold no profile for gets empty lists and a null photo_url.

namesakes.description: Bare-name searches: further verified people with the requested name. Not billed.

status.description: Whether additional discovery beyond the first pass was needed and finished.

source_counts.description: Evidence entries by source; ploid is the only key.

provider_outcomes.description: Empty when discovery was not needed; otherwise a single ploid entry.

total_time_ms.description: Total search processing time, including planning, retrieval and verification.

rejected.description: Present when the count fell short: how many evaluated people the verifier would not admit (reasons are not returned).

has_more.description: More candidates existed than were checked or returned.

verified_filters.description: Filters proven per person with evidence, such as experience.past_companies.

max_age_days.description: Maximum age, in days, of the cached evidence behind each result. May be fractional when derived.

source.description: request when the caller set freshness.max_age_days; default when derived from the request's time-sensitive facts.

score.description: Relative rank within this response on a 0..1 scale; 1 is the strongest match.

filter_match.description: One entry per requested filter, keyed by field (title, company) or path (experience.past_companies). indexed_field entries were checked against the stored profile; verified_evidence entries were proven by research, with matching evidence in verification.

observed.description: The profile value the filter was checked against.

matched.description: The any_of value or single filter value that matched.

criterion.description: The criterion verified for a filter the index cannot hold.

person_id.description: Stable Ploid identity. Deep person enrichment currently requires a linked LinkedIn profile.

profile_url.description: Canonical public profile or individual biography when discovered outside LinkedIn.

confidence.description: Relative rank within this response on a 0..1 scale; 1 is the strongest match.

contact_status.description: LinkedIn contact fields can be resolved through POST /v1/enrich. Results without LinkedIn report unavailable.

resolution_source.description: Always ploid. The other values are kept so clients built against earlier versions still parse.

location_match.description: Verified searches with a location: whether the person's own location names the requested place or only lies inside it.

positions.description: Present when contents.fields includes positions; most recent first.

SyncSearchPerson.description: Only resolved people are returned. Requested profile fields are present when selected and may be null when the people index has no value.

company_domain.description: The employer's website domain, e.g. stripe.com; use it for logos and matching.

started.description: YYYY-MM or YYYY as stated on the profile.

ended.description: YYYY-MM or YYYY; null while current or when not stated.

seniority.description: Seniority level of the role: Owner, Founder, C-Level, Partner, President/Vice President, Head, Director, Manager, Senior, Specialist or Intern; null when unknown.

department.description: Department of the role, e.g. Sales or Engineering; null when unknown.

school_domain.description: The school's website domain, e.g. mit.edu.

resolution_source.description: Always ploid. public_web is kept so clients built against earlier versions still parse.

next_offset.description: Search only: where the next page starts while the index still has matches.

criteria.description: Criteria every admitted row is verified against.

pricing.description: Estimate; billing settles on admitted rows.

items_url.description: Page admitted rows, usable while the search runs.

name.description: Full name; a partial or misspelled surname is tolerated.

company.description: Company name or web domain, such as Acme or acme.com.

address.description: Street or mailing address; it only has to fit the person's area.

work_email.description: Work email. Its domain identifies the employer unless it is a free mailbox provider.

phone.description: Phone number with 7 to 15 digits, in any common format.

profiles.description: Profiles found while resolving. Missing platforms are omitted; more_profiles shows how to look for more.

more_profiles.description: Present when found. A ready-to-send /v1/person request that looks for more public profiles.

name.description: When given, the person found must carry this name.

fast_only.description: Answer from Ploid's graph only (about a second) and skip the slower contact-network lookup.

positions.description: Work history, most recent first; empty when the profile is not in our people data.

query.example: New LinkedIn posts from Nvidia about AI chips

type.description: `text` returns `{ summary }` per item. `object` returns the schema you give or one derived from the query.

schema.description: JSON Schema with an object root, at most 25 properties.

description.description: Describe the fields in prose, or paste example JSON or a JSON Schema, to derive `schema`.

relevance_criteria.description: Every item must satisfy this to be emitted. Null emits all new activity.

kind.description: `company` is LinkedIn-only; elsewhere brand accounts are profiles.

identifier.description: Profile or company URL or @handle; search terms for keyword; tag without # for hashtag. Instagram supports hashtags but not keyword search.

events.description: Defaults to posts. Topics support posts only.

webhook_secret.description: Signs deliveries to webhook_url: `X-Ploid-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body>`.

cron.description: Five-field cron. The minute field must be a single value, so runs happen at most hourly.

status.description: `skipped` means available ACU or the API-key budget could not cover the run; `error` explains which.

webhook.description: Delivery of this run's event to the monitor's webhook_url; null when the monitor has none or the run sent no event.

relevant.description: Candidates that passed the relevance check; items holds the newest max_items_per_run of them.

already_seen.description: An earlier run already recorded this item, so a real run would not send it again.

MonitorItem.description: Webhook events: monitor.run.completed, monitor.run.failed, monitor.run.skipped. monitor.run.completed is sent only when a run emits items and carries up to 100 of them. Each run's delivery outcome is on the run ('webhook'); POST /v1/monitors/{id}/webhook/test sends a monitor.webhook.test event on demand.

output.description: Object matching the monitor's output schema, or null when extraction failed.

source.description: Normalized text, author, metrics and event details.

domain.description: The website's domain, such as acme.com or www.acme.com. Paths, ports, credentials, IP addresses and internal hosts are rejected.

freshness.description: How old a stored scan may be and still be served instead of a new scan (default 30 days). 0 asks for a new scan, except that a scan of the domain from the last 10 minutes is always served. meta.freshness echoes the window applied.

max_age_days.description: Maximum age, in days, of the cached evidence behind each returned result.

credits_charged.description: 0 when the result is not billable.

remaining_credits.description: The workspace's balance after the charge; only when something was charged.

canonical_domain.description: Where the homepage redirected, when that differs from domain.

status.description: assessed: the scan completed. partial: something was captured, but the scan was cut short or only DNS answered. blocked: the site refused the scan, or the domain opted out of crawling. failed: nothing usable came back.

scanned_at.description: Start time of the scan behind this result.

dns.description: Whether at least one DNS query returned records.

limits.description: Plain-language notes on anything that cut the scan or the result short.

versions.description: Opaque revision identifiers. Results with different versions may not be directly comparable.

assessment.description: observed: seen on the cited surface. configured: referenced or authorized (SPF, CSP). verification_only: only a verification token. content_candidate: named in page content. inferred: implied by an observed technology.

version.description: Set only when every sighting in this scope agrees.

inferred_from.description: Parent tech_ids of an inferred record; empty otherwise.

evidence.description: Where and when it was seen, each item a different source, type and match. Empty for inferred records.

source_url.description: The page or DNS name it was seen on, without query, fragment or credentials.

type.description: What it was seen in: a page's URL, markup, text, meta tags, scripts or stylesheets, a network request, a response header or cookie, robots.txt, the TLS certificate, or a DNS record (dns_spf is a TXT record holding an SPF policy). other: a kind this list does not name yet.

match.description: The part of a DNS record or certificate issuer that matched, not always the whole value. Null for website evidence.

role.description: The job, as a recruiter names it: "forklift operator", "journeyman electrician", "CDL A driver".

location.description: A US city and state: "Chambersburg, PA" or "Grand Rapids, Michigan".

radius_miles.description: Also search the towns within this many miles of the place. 0 searches the place alone.

include_related_roles.description: Also return adjacent jobs in the same trade family (reach truck operators and order pickers for a forklift search), ranked after the requested job.

sources.description: Where to look. linkedin: the maintained people index (current titles). facebook: a historical archive of US Facebook profiles whose workplace names the trade; its rows come back with freshness archived, a facebook_url and has_phone, and no LinkedIn.

offset.description: Workers to skip, for the next page. Pages run out at 600 workers per role and place; narrow the radius or role for more.

exact.description: Titles searched as the requested job.

related.description: Adjacent titles searched; empty when include_related_roles is false.

nearby.description: Towns within the radius that were searched.

candidates_seen.description: Candidates read from every source before title and place filtering.

has_more.description: More matching workers exist past this page; raise offset.

location_match.description: exact: the requested place; nearby: a town within the radius.

role_match.description: exact: a title meaning the requested job; related: an adjacent job in the same trade family.

matched_role.description: The searched title this person's title satisfied.

freshness.description: current: the maintained people index. archived: a one-time historical corpus; the title and place may be years old, verify before relying on them.

has_phone.description: Facebook-sourced rows only: the archive record carries a phone number. It is not revealed by this endpoint or by /v1/enrich yet.

socials.description: Other known public profile URLs by platform.

rows.description: At most 25 rows for sync requests.

deadline_ms.description: Sync only: cells not filled by then return status timeout. Ignored for async.

freshness.description: Oldest cached evidence reused without a live read; 0 re-reads everything. Omitted, each field uses its own window.

include_unverified.description: Also return the best value of unverified cells, with its confidence and evidence. They keep status unverified and are not billed; confidence folds in how likely the profile is the row's subject.

DatasetRowSeed.description: Identifies one row's subject. At least one of name, domain, linkedin_url, email, or a socials value is required.

linkedin_url.description: A LinkedIn person (/in/) or company (/company/) URL.

socials.description: Handles or profile URLs per platform, plus the subject's own website.

key.description: A built-in field for the entity type, or custom.<name> (1-60 lowercase letters, digits, or underscores).

description.description: Required for custom.* columns: what to find.

format.description: custom.* only; defaults to text. Built-in fields have a fixed format.

cells.description: One cell per requested column key.

value.description: The field's value when status is found (string, number, or object by format), or an unverified cell's best value when the request set include_unverified; null otherwise.

confidence.description: Agreement-weighted confidence; null when nothing was found.

status.description: found is billed; unverified means candidates disagreed or were too weak to return a value.

validation.description: Deliverability for found email.work, email.personal, and phone cells.

max_credits.description: Upper bound if every requested cell were found; reserved against the API key budget.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; null on the last page.

query.description: Free text over login, company, and repository names.

company.description: Company on the profile; known aliases also match.

repo_owner.description: Worked on any repository this user or organization owns.

has_email.description: Whether a public email was ever listed. The address itself is never returned.

active_since.description: Public activity on or after this date.

language.description: One of the account's ten most-used languages, for example Rust.

include_automation.description: Keep likely bot, CI, and release accounts, which are left out unless login is given.

limit.description: Page size. Defaults to 25, or 10 when include_profiles is true.

include_profiles.description: Attach live public profiles. Limits the page to 10.

repos.description: Up to 100 repositories worked on (owner/name). The repo filter searches all of them.

active_months.description: Months with at least one push, pull request, or review.

profile.description: Only with include_profiles: the live public profile, or null when GitHub returned none.

total.description: Matching accounts, counted exactly up to 10,000 (relation gte beyond that).

min_commits.description: At least this many commits pushed, 2011 through October 2025.

min_merged_pull_requests.description: At least this many authored pull requests merged, 2011 through October 2025.

min_recent_pushes.description: At least this many pushes in the 12 months before the index was built.

active_since.description: Public activity on or after this date.

language.description: One of the account's ten most-used languages, for example Rust.

include_automation.description: Keep likely bot, CI, and release accounts, which are left out unless login is given.

sort.description: relevance, or most commits, merged pull requests, recent pushes (recent_activity), or latest activity (last_active) first.

linkedin.description: Hard filters on the linked LinkedIn profile, as in POST /v1/search: one value, or any_of and none_of lists.

require_linkedin.description: Drop accounts that could not be tied to a LinkedIn profile.

repos.description: Up to 100 repositories worked on (owner/name). The repo filter searches all of them.

activity.description: Public activity from GH Archive; null when none is on record. Commits and pull requests cover 2011 through October 2025; pushes run to the index build.

pull_requests.description: Pull requests opened by this account.

merged_pull_requests.description: Pull requests opened by this account and merged.

active_months.description: Months with at least one push, pull request, or review.

profile.description: Only with include_profiles: the live public profile, or null when GitHub returned none.

indexed.description: False when the GitHub profile links a LinkedIn profile Ploid has not indexed yet.

scanned.description: GitHub accounts this page examined; next_offset advances by this.

platform.description: Use x for new integrations; twitter remains a compatibility alias.

identifier.description: Handle, vanity slug, or a profile URL belonging to the selected platform.

profile.description: Public profile fields vary by platform. Internal routing metadata is removed.

lastRefreshedAt.description: When this profile was last read from LinkedIn. Older than the request when a stored copy answered it.

companyUniversalName.description: The company page's vanity name, e.g. microsoft.

employmentType.description: As entered on the profile, e.g. Full-time; often empty.

workplaceType.description: On-site, Hybrid or Remote, as entered on the profile; often empty.

seniority.description: Seniority level of the role: Owner, Founder, C-Level, Partner, President/Vice President, Head, Director, Manager, Senior, Specialist or Intern; null when unknown.

department.description: Department of the role, e.g. Sales or Engineering; null when unknown.

kind.description: The site whose reader took the URL; null when unsupported.

data.description: The profile, present when status is ok.

CorpusSearchRequest.description: Provide either `query` or `filters` with at least one of title, company, school and location.

query.description: A plain-English description of the people to find.

keywords.description: Words the profile must contain, beside at least one other filter.

oneOf.description: Items joined with spaces must total at most 200 characters.

url.description: LinkedIn profile URL. Send it to /enrich as linkedin_url.

title.description: The job that matched the search, or the current job.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

data.description: Provider-neutral LinkedIn data. Fields vary by the selected read operation and internal credentials and status fields are removed.

EnrichContactRequest.description: Canonical contact-resolution contract for new integrations.

email.description: Email to look up from. With first_name and last_name at a work domain, Ploid searches by name at that company; otherwise, or when linkedin_url is requested, it first finds the person behind the email (reverse lookup).

EnrichLegacyRequest.description: Legacy lightweight profile/contact contract. New integrations should use EnrichContactRequest.

data.description: Only requested contact fields are present.

employer.description: work_email only: the employer the address belongs to, which may not be the requested company. `domain` is the address's domain; `name` is set only when the person's current employer owns that domain.

data.description: Only requested enrichment fields are present; an unavailable field is null.

acu_value_usd.description: Fixed USD value of one ACU.
